hooks.text: Betelgeuse is secretly an escaped runaway star barreling across the galaxy.
Why is a giant star barreling across the galaxy at thirty kilometers per second?
A runaway star is speeding through space at thirty kilometers per second.

title: The Escape of Orion's Giant Star
description: Betelgeuse was ejected from Orion's Belt and now plows through space at thirty kilometers per second with a massive bow shock.

beats.text: Betelgeuse is secretly an escaped runaway star barreling across the galaxy.
beats.visual: artist concept of runaway star Betelgeuse moving through interstellar space, 2012

beats.text: This red supergiant sits in the constellation Orion, normally ranking among the ten brightest stars in our night sky.
beats.visual: star map of constellation Orion highlighting red supergiant Betelgeuse, 2020

beats.text: If placed at the center of our solar system, its massive body would swallow Earth and stretch all the way out to Mars.
beats.visual: diagram comparing Betelgeuse size with the inner solar system, 2018
queries: Solar system vs Betelgeuse orbit illustration

beats.text: Millions of years ago, violent gravitational forces flung this giant out of its birthplace near Orion's Belt.
beats.visual: illustration of Orion's Belt stars and surrounding interstellar gas clouds, 2015

beats.text: Now, the ten-million-year-old star plows through the interstellar medium at thirty kilometers per second.
beats.visual: artist concept of runaway star plowing through interstellar gas, 2012

beats.text: As its powerful stellar wind slams into surrounding gas, it forms a gargantuan cosmic shockwave.
beats.visual: infrared image of Betelgeuse bow shock taken by Akari satellite, 2012

beats.text: Its collision with interstellar dust creates a glowing shield four light-years wide.
beats.visual: far-infrared image of the massive four light-year wide bow shock, 2012

beats.text: That is how a giant star became a celestial runaway.
beats.visual: wide constellation view of Orion with Betelgeuse at the shoulder, 2020
